chapter_note: This chapter is largely built from an older, systematic correspondential teaching that maps Sun/day/light and Night/darkness through numbered sets (seven goods, seven evils; five archetypes; three correspondences to the Father). A late hagiographic frame opens the chapter, and the end shows strong editorial/application drift: polemic against “the sects,” direct audience address/blessing, and an explicit ‘saviour’ saying (Gospel/Thomas vector) plus a “children of light/day” formula (Pauline-style). Paragraph 2 also shows a clear pivot from cosmic identification of the Sun to biblical-law polemic (Satan’s law), indicating later application grafted onto an older kernel.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic hagiographic setup: “Once again, the apostle…” sitting among disciples; narrative staging rather than impersonal exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: it is the gate of life and the vessel of peace, to this great aeon of light [...]. ⟨p.159⟩
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the subsequent polemical/biblical-law application about Satan placing a prohibition “in his law” (cosmos → contemporary scriptural institution), which is not part of the self-contained cosmic mapping of the Sun.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opens with a cosmic identification of the Sun (gate/vessel within the aeon of Light), then pivots to anti-law polemic anchored in “Satan… in his law” (later application/sectarian redaction).
Application voice and present anchoring (“even today”); rhetorical blame of people’s blindness rather than structural cosmological mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: Every day, would this great light-giver shine its light, it shall do seven good things for them. Shall they not see them?
paragraphs.temporal_note: Begins a numbered, systematic heptad (seven goods): a hallmark of the older teaching’s structured exposition, despite the rhetorical question.

paragraphs.core_text: The first good thing that it does for them is its light, which it shines upon them. It opens the eyes of all mankind. They see underfoot as they walk by it. It takes away the blindness of the night, which made them blind with its darkness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Part of the formal sevenfold sequence: impersonal description of effects of the Sun’s light against Night/darkness.

paragraphs.core_text: The second: When (the sun) is come to the world, with its coming it shall bring calm and peace to the entire world. With its coming it shall also take away from them all the fear and trembling, which their heart is filled with the whole night; for it shall take away the darkness present by its light, and sweep it out. Also, this is how it extinguishes fear by its calm.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the heptad; descriptive mechanism (light dispels darkness/fear) stays within the day–night correspondence.

paragraphs.core_text: The third is its vigil; because when (the sun) comes to the world all sleeping mankind shall arise and awake. And the watchmen too shall cease from watching. The guards who sit at the gates of camps, they break vigil at the watchposts, because of its light that has shone upon them in the world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Still within the sevenfold schema; functional description of ‘vigil’ as a property effected by sunrise (correspondential register).

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.160⟩ The fourth: It shall nourish, and give strength, taste and scent, to the trees and fruits and vegetables, and all the herbs, and the flowers and grasses, which are upon the entire earth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Correspondential sensory/register language (taste/scent/strength) tied to solar action; impersonal exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth: When (the sun) shines in all the world, the evil reptile and the sharp-toothed beasts that are filled of wickedness, they shall flee to hiding in their dens.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the systematic list; portrays light’s ordering power over hostile creatures as a cosmic-day effect.

paragraphs.core_text: The sixth: When it shines its light, the wound of any person is eased from pain. Its light shall melt away the evil arts of every doer of wickedness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Heptad continuation; light as healing/dispelling force (still descriptive, not addressed as command).

paragraphs.core_text: The seventh: (The sun) shall display and manifest to the world the sign of the splendour of the aeons of light, from which it has come out; it here in this world being their sign. It brings light to the whole of creation.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Explicitly correspondential: Sun as ‘sign’ of the Aeons of Light (cosmos→cosmos mapping).
Polemic against “sects of error” and evaluative rhetoric (“foolishness”); application layer rather than structural exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: the night, for it has all wickednesses therein. Every occasion, would the night fall, it shall do seven evils in the world.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the direct audience-address transition (“Now, just as I have shown you… hear also what I teach you…”), which is a rhetorical bridge from teacher to disciples rather than the impersonal teaching kernel.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Editorial discourse connective and first-person address introduce an otherwise old structural heptad (seven evils of Night).

paragraphs.core_text: The first wickedness that the night shall do in the world is the darkness, with which it shall fill the entire world; because when the sun sinks from the world and draws to it its rays, at that instant the shadow of the night shall spread out over the whole world. The eyes of the people fill with blackness. They neither see nor wonder with their eyes, because of the darkness of the night which shall fill the whole world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Begins the Night heptad in the same systematic mode; descriptive causal language (sun withdraws → shadow spreads).

paragraphs.core_text: The second evil thing that the night shall do is its fear; because when its shadow looms forth, its fear and its trembling shall possess all of mankind. The entire world shall fill of the night.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered continuation; fear as a property of Night (correspondential register).

paragraphs.core_text: The third: When the night falls, all creatures take up revolt. They rebel in their heart, to do wickedness and perdition.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Heptad continuation; Night’s moral/affective effect presented as an impersonal cosmic condition.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth: The heaviness of sleep shall lay upon them, and they fall asleep; they slumber and doze, and they are like these corpses in the night.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the structured list; sleep as a ‘heaviness’ (quality/archetype register).

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth is its ugliness; again, when the night would fall, the form of the people shall be hidden in the darkness and the ugliness of the night. The beauty and the form of men and women shall not be displayed before one another, because of its darkness and its ugliness, which it shall spread out over all their forms.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered quality (‘ugliness’) mapped to Night’s obscuring action; stays within day/night phenomenology used as correspondence.

paragraphs.core_text: The sixth occasion is when the night would fall on the world. At that instant evil people shall come out to do wickedness; the adulterers, and the robbers and poisoners. The evil beasts shall come out, and all the reptiles that are filled with wickedness, from their dens. And they stalk in the night. Also, the demons and fiends find power to do wickedness in the night. Again, the blows and buffets and wounds and discharges shall torment people in the night; because in it the whole of evil shall find strength.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Still integrated into the numbered heptad as a descriptive ‘night releases evil’ mechanism; no direct exhortation, though it uses social exempla.

paragraphs.core_text: The seventh: The night shall display the sign of the Darkness, its father. It has arisen out of its essence; because this night that came out of this first Darkness has been displayed in the world. Note this night, the shadow of this first Darkness, the one that is entwined and bound in all things above and below.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Explicit cosmos→cosmos correspondence: Night as ‘sign/shadow’ of primordial Darkness (personified source).
Recap plus polemic against “the sects” (they have not seen/known); shifts from impersonal schema to evaluative application.

paragraphs.core_text: There are five archetypes occur in the sun, it making them [...] as it finds the world.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/frame attribution (“Once again… He says to his disciples:”), a compilation-layer speech marker.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Clear frame intrusion (“he says to his disciples”) introducing a structured pentad of ‘archetypes’—the teaching kernel is the numbered schema.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.162⟩ The first is its light; for it illumines by its light the world, and all the creatures who exist in it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pentad continuation; archetype defined by function in the created order.

paragraphs.core_text: The second is its beauty; because when it shines, it shall flood beauty and loveliness upon all creatures and everything.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pentad continuation; beauty as a radiated quality.

paragraphs.core_text: The third is its peace; for, again, when the sun would shine on the world, all people shall receive affection through it, and give peace to one another.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pentad continuation; social harmony presented as an effect/property of Sun (still descriptive, not exhortative).

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth is the life of the living soul, which it shall release from all the bonds and fetters of heaven and earth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmological soteriology (living soul; bonds of heaven/earth) presented as an archetypal function of the Sun.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth: It gives a strength to the elements; and also it gives a scent and a taste to the entire Cross of the Light.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Strong correspondential register (elements; scent/taste) plus Manichaean cosmic structure (Cross of the Light).

paragraphs.core_text: its light illumines more than all lights that occur in the world. Also, its beauty is more beautiful than all the beauties of mankind. Again, its peace is more surpassing than all the powers and guards who exist in the world. Its releasing action, by which it releases the living soul, is a full day ahead of all releasing actions! The strength that it gives to its limbs is a great strength, being mightier than all strengths!
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the immediate audience-address proem (“So, you yourselves see that…”), which shifts from impersonal exposition into rhetorical appeal.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Comparative amplification of the pentad’s archetypes; contains rhetorical address but preserves a coherent teaching kernel summarizing the five qualities.

paragraphs.core_text: Once again, there are another three archetypes made apparent by the sun, in respect of the mystery of the first greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Introduces a new structured triad tied to the ‘mystery of the first greatness’ (systematic cosmological setup).

paragraphs.core_text: The first is the filling up of the disk of its ship; because its ship has filled up every season, and shall not wane at all, the way that the ship of the moon wanes. This continuous filling, by which it is filled, displays the mystery of the Father, the great greatness; from whom all the powers and the gods have come forth. He shall never wane, nor shall lack ever exist in him!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Direct correspondence: solar ‘ship’ fullness ↔ Father’s inexhaustibility; cosmic beings (‘powers and the gods’) remain internal to the system.

paragraphs.core_text: The second: (The sun's) light surpasses the light of all the stars, and all the lights that occur in the universe; corresponding to the mystery of the light of the Father; for his light surpasses and is greater than the light of his aeons.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Explicit ‘corresponding to’ formula within cosmology; no external institutional target.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.163⟩ The third: This sun is very high above all else. It surpasses the height of all the mountains and hills that exist upon the entire earth, corresponding to the mystery of the Father of Greatness; for he is high above all the household of his light-earth. Also, because the Father himself is high above all the heights and the mountains of his light-earth. He is 'filled up' in his image [all] the time and every hour from eternity to eternity!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Triadic correspondence continues; strongly internal cosmic geography (‘light-earth’) and Father of Greatness language marks the old systematic layer.
High application voice: direct address (“O my beloved ones!”), polemic against sects; recap framed for persuasion rather than exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: The mystery of the first great light is the sun, which is this second light-giver, the one that comes daily to the world. It displays all the marks of its graces, displaying and signifying on its own behalf that it is good, out of the essence of the good. It came from the good Father and appeared in this world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic identification of the Sun within a graded light hierarchy (first/second light-giver) and origin-from-Father explanation; remains cosmos→cosmos.

paragraphs.core_text: In contrast, this night that is made of fear exists after the mystery of the darkness. Behold too the mystery of its essence! It displays it in the world in all these wickednesses.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the concluding polemical application (“but the sects know it not… They do not distinguish…”), which targets contemporary opponents rather than describing the cosmic correspondence itself.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Begins as a pure correspondence statement (Night after Darkness), then shifts into anti-sect rhetoric; the latter is a later applicative layer.
Explicit ‘saviour’ allusion and a quoted saying (Gospel of Thomas vector): material entered via Christian gospel tradition, regardless of correspondential content.
“Once again the apostle speaks” + ‘children of the day/light’ formula aligns with Pauline/NT idiom; enters through Christian overlay and compilation speech framing.
Closing benediction/exhortation to “beloved ones” with salvation payoff (“inherit life eternal”); application-layer homiletic ending consistent with editorial fatigue toward chapter end.
